answer: Cross-Epoch Trace Matching. Each identity submits prior-epoch action features: timing, interaction motifs, resource sequence. At rollover, similarity to its own history must exceed a fixed threshold to continue; new identities serve one probation epoch. An attacker must run every Sybil through probation and keep traces consistent, paying sustained compute and recurring transaction fees per identity. A knoll of idle accounts does not bypass this. Spawned identities cannot cheaply cross the ocean of epochs without matching histories. To forge many consistent traces costs per-identity work.
